fix.cli: run this over USB with --connection usb
fix.mcp: connect over USB ('usb') to change {setting}, or ask the user to do it at the pod

BP0044.name: policy_loosen_usb_only
BP0044.message: Only the USB console can loosen {setting} (now {now})
BP0044.cause: The cloud may make the pod stricter but never looser: a stolen cloud account must not be able to lower the pod's firmware signature policy.

fix.sdk: loosen {setting} on the pod's USB console
fix.cli: loosen {setting} over USB with `benchpod policy` and --connection usb

BP0045.name: role_required
BP0045.message: {cmd} needs an organization owner or admin
BP0045.cause: A cloud session runs commands up to the tier the server allows its user. {cmd} changes or updates the pod, which needs an owner or admin of the pod's organization.

fix.sdk: use an API key or session of an organization owner or admin (API keys need the benchpod:admin scope)
fix.cli: sign in as an organization owner or admin; API keys need the benchpod:admin scope
fix.mcp: tell the user {cmd} needs an organization owner or admin (an API key with the benchpod:admin scope)

BP0046.name: no_analog_front_end
BP0046.message: This BenchPod has no analog front end, so it cannot run {cmd}
BP0046.cause: The digital board has no DAC, ADC or analog outputs. The pod checks at boot; after fitting an analog add-on, restart it.

fix.sdk: use a pod with an analog front end (bp.capabilities shows it), or leave out the analog step
fix.cli: use a pod with an analog front end
fix.mcp: this pod has no analog front end; skip the analog step or use another pod
fix.web: This pod has no analog front end.

BP0047.name: pod_busy
BP0047.message: The pod is running another long command (a capture, measurement, upload or update)
BP0047.cause: Captures, measurements, waveform uploads and firmware updates share the pod's sample memory, so one runs at a time. Light commands (status, GPIO, ...) still run.

fix.sdk: wait for the other command to finish, then try again
fix.cli: the pod is running another long command; try again when it ends
fix.mcp: wait for the other call to finish, then try again
fix.web: The pod is busy with another capture or upload. Try again when it ends.

BP0048.name: storage_bus_busy
BP0048.message: The pod's storage bus is in use: {what}
BP0048.cause: The flash that holds settings, gateware and update images shares a bus with the sample memory. While {what}, the pod cannot write it.

fix.sdk: try again when it ends
fix.cli: try again when it ends
fix.mcp: wait until it ends, then try again
fix.web: Try again when it ends.

BP0049.name: uart_session_open
BP0049.message: A UART session is already open
BP0049.cause: The pod runs one UART at a time: the web app's Terminal, a test, an MCP session or a flash over the UART holds it.

BP0050.name: swd_session_open
BP0050.message: An SWD session is already running
BP0050.cause: The pod runs one SWD session (a flash or a debug run) at a time.

fix.sdk: wait for the running flash to finish, then try again
fix.cli: wait for the running flash to finish, then try again
fix.mcp: wait for the running flash to finish, then try again
fix.web: Wait for the running flash to finish.

BP0051.name: update_in_progress
BP0051.message: A {target} update from {holder} is in progress
BP0051.cause: The pod takes one update at a time, from one place. Another one is running.

fix.sdk: wait for the other update to finish (or ota_abort it from where it runs), then try again
fix.cli: wait for the other update to finish, then try again
fix.mcp: tell the user another update is running and wait for it
fix.web: Another update is running. Wait for it to finish.

BP0052.name: cloud_command_busy
BP0052.message: The pod is still running the previous cloud command
BP0052.cause: Over the cloud command channel the pod runs one command at a time. The server retries, so this is usually brief.

fix.sdk: try again in a moment
fix.cli: try again in a moment
fix.mcp: retry in a moment
fix.web: Try again in a moment.

BP0053.name: reply_too_large
BP0053.message: The reply did not fit the pod's reply buffer
BP0053.cause: The command worked, but its answer is larger than the pod can send at once. Commands that can grow (la_pins) take a subset.

fix.sdk: ask for less at once (bp.la_pins(la=[...]) reads a subset); update the SDK if it keeps happening
fix.cli: ask for less at once; update the CLI if it keeps happening
fix.mcp: ask for fewer channels or less data per call

BP0054.name: cloud_reply_too_large
BP0054.message: The reply is too large for the cloud channel ({bytes} bytes, limit {limit})
BP0054.cause: Cloud command replies travel in one frame of at most {limit} bytes. This one is {bytes}. Large data (captures) go through the cloud byte tunnel instead.

fix.sdk: ask for less at once (bp.la_pins(la=[...]) reads a subset), or connect over the LAN or USB
fix.cli: ask for less at once, or connect over the LAN or USB
fix.mcp: ask for fewer channels or less data per call
fix.web: Ask for less at once.

BP0055.name: sensor_instance_unknown
BP0055.message: The pod has no emulated sensor {instance}
BP0055.cause: The instance was never defined or started on this pod, was stopped, or the pod restarted.

fix.sdk: list the running sensors with bp.sensors.status(), or start {instance} first
fix.cli: list the running sensors with `benchpod sensor status`, or start {instance} first
fix.mcp: call sensor_status to list the running sensors, or sensor_start {instance} first
fix.web: {instance} is not running. Start it first.

BP0056.name: no_module_link
BP0056.message: This BenchPod has no module link, so it cannot run {cmd}
BP0056.cause: Only boards with a module header (digital v3r3) talk to an add-on module.

fix.sdk: skip the module step on this board
fix.cli: this board has no module link
fix.mcp: this pod has no module link; skip the module step
fix.web: This pod has no module link.

BP0057.name: image_switch_sensors_running
BP0057.message: The emulated sensors {sensors} need the emulation image; stop them before switching
BP0057.cause: I2C, SPI and UART sensors run in the emulation gateware image. Switching to another image would stop them mid-run, so the pod refuses.

fix.sdk: stop them with bp.sensors.stop(), then switch the image
fix.cli: stop them with `benchpod sensor stop` first
fix.mcp: call sensor_stop (all) first, then fpga_image
fix.web: Stop the emulated sensors first.

BP0058.name: fpga_image_required
BP0058.message: {feature} is not in the running gateware image; it needs the {image} image
BP0058.cause: The pod's FPGA runs one of three images (loop, deep replay, emulation), and each has some features. {feature} is in the {image} image.

fix.sdk: switch with bp.fpga_image(FpgaImage.LOOP) (or DEEP_REPLAY for the deep image), then try again
fix.cli: switch with `benchpod sensor image {image}`, then try again
fix.mcp: call fpga_image(image="{image}"), then try again
fix.web: Switch the FPGA image to {image} first.

BP0059.name: fpga_image_sensors_first
BP0059.message: {feature} is not in the emulation image the emulated sensors use; stop them, then switch to the {image} image
BP0059.cause: Emulated I2C, SPI and UART sensors run in the emulation gateware image, which has no room for {feature}. It needs the {image} image, and switching stops the sensors.

fix.sdk: bp.sensors.stop(), then bp.fpga_image(...) for the {image} image
fix.cli: stop the sensors with `benchpod sensor stop`, then switch with `benchpod sensor image {image}`
fix.mcp: call sensor_stop (all), then fpga_image(image="{image}")
fix.web: Stop the emulated sensors, then switch to the {image} image.

BP0060.name: ota_unknown_target
BP0060.message: {target} is not an update target this firmware knows
BP0060.cause: The firmware on the pod is older than the tool, or the target name is wrong.

fix.sdk: update the pod's firmware first (`benchpod flash-self`)
fix.cli: update the pod's firmware with `benchpod flash-self` first
fix.mcp: tell the user the pod's firmware does not know this update target; update the firmware first
fix.web: Update the pod's firmware first.

BP0061.name: i2c_needs_pullups
BP0061.message: I2C needs pull-ups: LA{la} has none switched on
BP0061.cause: I2C lines are open drain: something must pull them high. The pod can do it with its own pull-ups, or the board has its own.

fix.sdk: switch the pull-up on (bp.enable_pullup({la})), or pass pullups="external" when the board has its own
fix.cli: pull LA{la} up with `benchpod la pull {la} up`, or pass --pullups external when the board has its own
fix.mcp: call set_pull(las=[{la}], pull="up"), or pass pullups="external" when the board has its own
fix.web: Switch on LA{la}'s pull-up, or say the board has its own.

BP0062.name: i2c_session_not_open
BP0062.cause: I2C transactions run inside a session that i2c_start opens.

fix.sdk: open one with bp.open_i2c() first
fix.cli: start the I2C master first
fix.mcp: call i2c_open first
fix.web: Open an I2C session first.

BP0063.name: i2c_engine_reset
BP0063.message: The I2C engine was reset, which ended the session
BP0063.cause: A gateware reload (an image switch, a recovery) resets the I2C engine, so the open session is gone.

fix.sdk: open the session again with bp.open_i2c()
fix.cli: start the I2C command again
fix.mcp: call i2c_open again
fix.web: Open the I2C session again.

BP0064.name: loop_sweep_with_map
BP0064.message: The sweep input cannot be combined with an input map on this gateware
BP0064.cause: The sweep spans the raw count range, not the mapped window, so most of each pass would sit at one end of the curve.

fix.sdk: step the input with bp.loop_input() instead of the sweep
fix.cli: step the loop input instead of using the sweep
fix.mcp: step the input with loop_input instead
fix.web: Step the input instead of sweeping it.

BP0065.name: output_used_by_sensor
BP0065.message: The {output} output is played by the emulated sensor {instance}
BP0065.cause: An analog emulated sensor drives the pod's {output} output, so a DAC or current command would fight it.

fix.sdk: stop it first with bp.sensors.stop("{instance}")
fix.cli: stop it first with `benchpod sensor stop {instance}`
fix.mcp: call sensor_stop(instance="{instance}") first
fix.web: Stop the emulated sensor {instance} first.

BP0066.name: step_busy
BP0066.message: A step pulse train is running
BP0066.cause: The pod runs one step train at a time.

fix.sdk: wait for the step train to finish (or stop it), then try again
fix.cli: wait for the step train to finish, then try again
fix.mcp: wait for the la_step train to finish, then try again
fix.web: Wait for the step train to finish.

BP0067.name: samples_out_of_range
BP0067.message: samples must be 1 to {max} for this capture
BP0067.cause: Each capture holds a fixed number of samples: the shallow ADC capture what fits the RAM buffer, the deep ones what fits their PSRAM region at the rate asked for. A deep ADC capture is capture_dual with la_samples 0.

fix.sdk: ask for at most {max} samples, or use a deep capture (capture_dual) for more
fix.cli: ask for at most {max} samples
fix.mcp: ask for at most {max} samples, or use capture_correlated / a deep capture for more
fix.web: Capture at most {max} samples.

BP0068.name: la_rate_above_ceiling
BP0068.message: LA at {rate_mhz} MS/s does not fit: with ADC samples in the capture the raw LA runs at most {max_mhz} MS/s on this gateware, {fit_mhz} MS/s for {samples} samples
BP0068.cause: On gateware before v53 the raw LA runs at most {max_mhz} MS/s when the same capture records ADC samples: faster, the PSRAM writer starved the ADC. The pod refuses an explicit rate it cannot run instead of slowing it down. {fit_mhz} MS/s is the fastest rate that fits {samples} samples. Above 12 MS/s the LA records its changes instead.

fix.sdk: ask for at most {max_mhz} MS/s ({fit_mhz} MS/s for {samples} samples), leave the rate out for the fastest that fits, or update the pod's gateware
fix.cli: ask for at most {max_mhz} MS/s, or leave the rate out for the fastest that fits
fix.mcp: retry with la_sample_rate_hz at most {fit_mhz} MHz in Hz (or leave it out for the fastest that fits)
fix.web: Pick {fit_mhz} MS/s or less, or leave the rate on automatic.

BP0069.name: la_rate_too_deep
BP0069.message: LA at {rate_mhz} MS/s does not fit {samples} samples: at most {max_samples} samples at {rate_mhz} MS/s, or at most {fit_mhz} MS/s for {samples} samples
BP0069.cause: The raw LA samples into a burst buffer that drains to the PSRAM more slowly than the fastest rates. A capture deeper than the buffer holds at {rate_mhz} MS/s would drop samples, so the pod refuses it instead of slowing it down. Either way out works: fewer samples at this rate, or a lower rate for this depth.

fix.sdk: capture at most {max_samples} samples at {rate_mhz} MS/s, or at most {fit_mhz} MS/s for {samples} samples (leave the rate out for the fastest that fits)
fix.cli: capture at most {max_samples} samples at {rate_mhz} MS/s, or ask for {fit_mhz} MS/s or less (or leave the rate out)
fix.mcp: retry with at most {max_samples} samples, or with the rate at most {fit_mhz} MS/s (or leave it out for the fastest that fits)
fix.web: Capture at most {max_samples} samples at {rate_mhz} MS/s, or pick {fit_mhz} MS/s or less.

BP0070.name: capture_dual_too_deep
BP0070.message: capture_dual takes at most {la_max} LA and {adc_max} ADC samples
BP0070.cause: Each stream of a capture_dual has its own PSRAM region of a fixed size. A deeper LA-only capture fits la_capture, which takes up to {la_capture_max} LA samples.

fix.sdk: ask for at most {la_max} LA and {adc_max} ADC samples, or use la_capture for up to {la_capture_max} LA samples
fix.cli: ask for at most {la_max} LA and {adc_max} ADC samples
fix.mcp: ask for at most {la_max} LA and {adc_max} ADC samples, or use capture_la for up to {la_capture_max} LA samples
fix.web: Capture at most {la_max} LA and {adc_max} ADC samples.

BP0071.name: capture_overflowed
BP0071.message: The capture overflowed: the PSRAM could not keep up with LA {la_ksps} kS/s and ADC {adc_ksps} kS/s
BP0071.cause: The capture started, but its streams wrote to the PSRAM faster than it could take them, so samples were lost and the pod returns none.

fix.sdk: lower la_sample_rate_hz or adc_sample_rate_hz, or capture fewer samples
fix.cli: lower the LA or ADC rate, or capture fewer samples
fix.mcp: retry with a lower la_sample_rate_hz or adc_sample_rate_hz, or fewer samples
fix.web: Lower the LA or ADC rate, or capture fewer samples.

BP0072.name: psram_too_small
BP0072.message: The capture is too deep: LA, ADC and a loaded DAC waveform together exceed the 8 MB PSRAM
BP0072.cause: A capture_dual packs its LA region, its ADC region and any deep-replay waveform still loaded into the pod's 8 MB PSRAM, and refuses up front when they do not fit.

fix.sdk: capture fewer LA or ADC samples, or free the replay waveform (bp.dac_stop()) first
fix.cli: capture fewer samples
fix.mcp: retry with fewer la_samples or adc_samples, or call dac_stop to free a loaded replay waveform
fix.web: Capture fewer samples, or stop the DAC replay first.

BP0073.name: psram_bandwidth
BP0073.message: The combined sample rate is more than the PSRAM bus can take
BP0073.cause: The LA, the ADC and a running deep replay share one PSRAM bus. The pod adds up their sustained rates and refuses a capture that would overrun it, instead of losing samples.

fix.sdk: lower la_sample_rate_hz or adc_sample_rate_hz, or stop the DAC replay first
fix.cli: lower the LA or ADC rate
fix.mcp: retry with a lower la_sample_rate_hz or adc_sample_rate_hz, or call dac_stop first
fix.web: Lower the LA or ADC rate, or stop the DAC replay first.

BP0074.name: signatures_always_required
BP0074.message: {setting} cannot be set to {want}: this firmware installs only signed images
BP0074.cause: Firmware 4.0.0 and later take an update (firmware, gateware, the Wi-Fi chip's image) only with a good signature, on every path: the LAN, the USB network adapter and the cloud. No command loosens that. Dev builds also take images signed with the developer key. Firmware you built yourself goes in over USB DFU (`benchpod flash-self`), which needs the pod on a USB cable.

fix.sdk: install a signed release, or install self-built firmware over USB DFU (`benchpod flash-self`)
fix.cli: install a signed release, or install self-built firmware over USB DFU with `benchpod flash-self` (without --network)
fix.mcp: tell the user the pod takes only signed images; self-built firmware goes in over USB DFU (`benchpod flash-self`)
fix.web: The pod takes only signed images. Install self-built firmware over USB with `benchpod flash-self`.

BP0075.name: lan_plaintext_off
BP0075.message: The pod serves its JSON API on the LAN over TLS only (port 8443): plaintext port 8080 is off
BP0075.cause: Firmware 4.0.0 and later serve the JSON API over Ethernet and Wi-Fi on TLS port 8443 only. Plaintext port 8080 still answers on the USB network adapter, and from the LAN when SCPI is switched on, but only for SCPI there. Plaintext JSON on the LAN comes back only when it is switched on over USB or from the cloud.

fix.sdk: connect to the pod by its address without a port (the SDK uses TLS on 8443 and pins the pod's certificate), or over USB ('usb')
fix.cli: connect by the pod's address without a port (the CLI uses TLS on 8443), or with --connection usb
fix.mcp: connect to the pod's address without :8080 (TLS on 8443 is used), or to 'usb'
fix.web: Connect to the pod over TLS (port 8443) or USB.

BP0076.name: usb_host_over_usb
BP0076.message: USB host mode cannot start over the pod's own USB link
BP0076.cause: While the pod hosts a board on its USB port it is off the computer's USB, so the connection that asked would drop before the answer arrives. USB host mode starts only over the network (LAN or Wi-Fi) or the cloud.

fix.sdk: connect to the pod over the network or the cloud (Client(host) or 'embeddedci:<name>'), not 'usb', then start USB host mode again
fix.cli: connect to the pod over the network or the cloud (--connection <host> or embeddedci:<name>), not usb, then run the command again
fix.mcp: connect to the pod over the network or the cloud (connect with its host or 'embeddedci:<name>'), not 'usb', then try again
fix.web: Connect to the pod over the network or the cloud to use USB host mode.

BP0077.name: usb_host_port_unavailable
BP0077.message: This pod has no USB host port {port}
BP0077.cause: Only pods with a USB-A host port can host a board there. Every pod can host on its USB-C port, but only on a bench rig with an adapter cable that powers the pod and carries the data lines to the board under test.

fix.sdk: use port='usb_c' with a USB-C adapter rig, or a pod with the USB-A host port
fix.cli: use --port usb_c with a USB-C adapter rig, or a pod with the USB-A host port
fix.mcp: tell the user this pod has no USB-A host port; port 'usb_c' works only with a USB-C adapter rig
fix.web: This pod has no USB-A host port.

BP0078.name: usb_host_no_crystal
BP0078.message: USB host mode needs the pod's crystal clock, which is not running
BP0078.cause: A USB host keeps the bus timing itself and needs a precise clock. The pod runs on its internal oscillator because the crystal did not start at boot.

fix.sdk: power cycle the pod; if bp.status() still shows the internal clock, contact support
fix.cli: power cycle the pod; if `benchpod status` still shows the internal clock, contact support
fix.mcp: ask the user to power cycle the pod; if it keeps happening, the pod needs support
fix.web: Power cycle the pod. If this keeps happening, contact support.

BP0079.name: usb_host_other_port
BP0079.message: USB host mode is already running on {port}
BP0079.cause: The pod hosts one port at a time. A start for the same port renews the timeout; another port needs a stop first.

fix.sdk: stop USB host mode first (enabled=False), then start it on the other port
fix.cli: stop USB host mode first, then start it on the other port
fix.mcp: stop USB host mode first, then start it on the other port
fix.web: Stop USB host mode first.

BP0080.name: dac_pinout_mismatch
BP0080.message: {cmd} refused, the DAC is off: the digital board ({digital}) and the analog module ({module}) use different flat-cable pinouts
BP0080.cause: The flat cable between the two boards carries the DAC's clock and data. Digital board v3r4 and analog module 3.5 swapped those two lines, so a newer board paired with an older one would send the DAC scrambled data and its outputs could jump to any voltage. The pod refuses every command that drives the DAC and sends it nothing; everything else keeps working. The module's revision comes from its EEPROM, so a module that was never programmed counts as an older one.

fix.sdk: pair a digital v3r4 or later board with an analog module 3.5 or later (or both older), or, if the module's EEPROM revision is wrong, program the revision printed on its board and restart the pod
fix.cli: pair a digital v3r4 or later board with an analog module 3.5 or later (or both older); `benchpod status` shows both. If the module's revision is wrong, program the one printed on its board and restart the pod
fix.mcp: tell the user the digital board and the analog module do not belong together (status shows both revisions): a digital v3r4+ board needs an analog module 3.5+, and an older digital board an older module
fix.web: The digital board and the analog module do not belong together, so the analog outputs are off. A digital v3r4 or later board needs an analog module 3.5 or later.
